line: Crowley gives Hod the number 8 and Mercury, airy and mercurial; Jung names Hod as the left, feminine side that Yesod unites with Nezach.

sections.title: Crowley's Eights
sections.line: The four Eights are attributed to Hod, and the number Eight, Hod, represents Mercury.

quotes.quote: The four Eights are attributed to Hod.
The number Eight, Hod, is very helpful in this card, because it represents Mercury in
The Eight of Wands is called Swiftness, as one might expect from its attribution to Mercury and Sagittarius.

sections.title: Mercury on the Tree
sections.line: Crowley names Hod as Mercury on the Tree and calls it airy and mercurial. The field's Mercurius is the quicksilver spirit; the sky layer ties the planet Mercury to that node.

quotes.quote: coin in the place of Hod (Mercury) on the Tree is marked with the cipher of the Sun.
for the Sephira Hod, which in our system is Airy and Mercurial

sections.title: Jung's Hod
sections.line: Jung's passage on Hod is ¶635, the same passage as Nezach: the left, feminine side of beauty.

quotes.quote: Yesod unites the emanation of the right, masculine side (Nezach, life-force) with the left, feminine side (Hod, beauty)
